# Temple Scroll Column 64 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 64 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**64:1** Do not neglect the Levites living in your towns, since they have no land allotment of their own among you.

**64:2** At the end of every three years, bring out the entire tithe from that year's harvest and store it in your towns.

**64:3** Then the Levites, who own no land among you, along with the foreigners, orphans, and widows living in your towns, may come and eat until they are satisfied,

**64:4** and I will bless everything you do.

**64:5** Every seven years you must cancel debts. Here is how the cancellation works: every creditor must forgive what he has loaned to his fellow Israelite. He must not demand repayment from his neighbor or brother,

**64:6** because my release has been proclaimed. You may collect debts from foreigners, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.

**64:7** If anyone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and enslaving or selling that person, the kidnapper must be put to death. You must purge this evil from among you.

**64:8** When someone has committed a capital crime and is executed, and his body is displayed by hanging on a tree,

**64:9** you must not leave the body hanging overnight. You must bury him that same day, because anyone who is hung up is under God's curse.

**64:10** You must not defile the land I am giving you as your inheritance.

**64:11** If a man betrays his own people by acting as a spy and handing them over to a foreign power, committing treason against his people,

**64:12** you shall hang him on a tree and let him die there. On the evidence of two or three witnesses

**64:13** he shall be condemned, and they shall hang him on the tree.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 64 is explosive. Lines 64:11–13 prescribe hanging ALIVE — not as post-mortem display but as the execution method itself. This is a radical reinterpretation of Deuteronomy's law. The crime is treason: betraying Israel to foreign powers. This text stood behind the controversy when the Hasmonean king Alexander Jannaeus crucified 800 opponents in 88 BCE — an event the Nahum Commentary calls "hanging men alive." The early Christian reading of "cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" (Gal 3:13) gains entirely new dimensions when read against this Qumran text.*
